Fetch taxonomic and functional profiles

Source: R/v2_fetch.R
fetchStudies.Rd

Fetch taxonomic and functional profiles

Usage

fetchStudies(
  study.ids,
  type = "SSU",
  samples = FALSE,
  biosamples = FALSE,
  studies = FALSE,
  analyses = FALSE,
  assemblies = FALSE,
  qc = FALSE
)

fetchAnalyses(
  analysis.ids,
  type = "SSU",
  samples = FALSE,
  biosamples = FALSE,
  studies = FALSE,
  analyses = FALSE,
  assemblies = FALSE,
  qc = FALSE
)

Arguments

study.ids

A character vector specifying study accessions, e.g., "MGYS00005116", or a data.frame returned by searchStudies.

type

A character vector specifying the profiles to fetch, e.g., "SSU" or c("SSU", "GO-slim"). See details for the types. (By default: type = "SSU")

samples

TRUE or FALSE specifying whether to add the sample metadata in MGnify. (By default: samples = FALSE)

biosamples

TRUE or FALSE specifying whether to add the attributes of the samples in BioSamples. (By default: biosamples = FALSE)

studies

TRUE or FALSE specifying whether to add the details and publications of the studies. (By default: studies = FALSE)

analyses

TRUE or FALSE specifying whether to add the details of the analyses, e.g., the quality control of pipeline v6. (By default: analyses = FALSE)

assemblies

TRUE or FALSE specifying whether to add the details of the assemblies. (By default: assemblies = FALSE)

qc

TRUE or FALSE specifying whether to add the quality control of pipelines v1-v5, e.g., the number of sequences before and after quality filtering. It is read from separate files, which makes the search slower. The details of the analyses are added too. (By default: qc = FALSE)

analysis.ids

A character vector specifying analysis accessions, e.g., "MGYA00383350", or a data.frame returned by searchAnalyses. Giving the data.frame is faster.

Value

For a single type, a TreeSummarizedExperiment with

  • assay: "counts"

  • colData: the columns of searchAnalyses, i.e., the metadata of the analyses, their studies and samples

  • rowData: taxonomy ranks, or the descriptions of the rows of functional profiles

For multiple types, a MultiAssayExperiment with a TreeSummarizedExperiment for each type that has data. The profiles are linked by sample, e.g., the SSU profile of an amplicon analysis and the GO profile of a metagenomic analysis of the same sample.

NULL is returned if no data could be fetched.

Details

fetchStudies fetches all the analyses of the given studies, and fetchAnalyses fetches specific analyses, e.g., a filtered result of searchAnalyses. Columns are analyses and rows are taxa or, in functional profiles, functions, e.g., GO terms. Taxa are matched across studies by their taxonomy lineage.

type tells which profile is fetched. Only analyses that have the type are fetched.

  • Taxonomic profiles: "SSU" and "LSU" (small and large subunit rRNA), "mOTUs" (marker genes of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes, pipelines v5-v6), "UNITE" and "ITSoneDB" (fungal ITS), "PR2" (eukaryotes), "DADA2-SILVA" and "DADA2-PR2" (amplicon sequence variants, pipeline v6), and "contigs" (number of contigs per taxon in assemblies, pipeline v6). Pipelines v1-v3 have a single profile, which is fetched with "SSU".

  • Functional profiles of metagenomes, metatranscriptomes and assemblies: "InterPro", "GO" and "GO-slim" (pipelines v1-v6), "Pfam" and "KO" (KEGG orthologs, pipelines v5-v6), and "antiSMASH" (biosynthetic gene clusters of assemblies, pipelines v5-v6). In pipeline v6, only assemblies have functional profiles.

Profiles of different pipeline versions are based on different reference databases, so they might not be directly comparable. To fetch a single pipeline version, subset the result of searchAnalyses by pipeline_version. Data is cached for the R session; to keep it between sessions, set options(MGnifyR.cache = "path/to/cache").

The arguments samples, biosamples, studies, analyses, assemblies and qc choose the metadata in colData, as in searchAnalyses. In fetchAnalyses, they are used only if analysis.ids are accessions; for a data.frame, give them to searchAnalyses instead.

See also

searchStudies

Examples

# Fetch all analyses of a study
tse <- fetchStudies("MGYS00005116")
#> Fetching 2 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.
#> The data includes analyses from multiple pipeline versions (V4.1, V5, V6). Their profiles are based on different reference databases. Consider subsetting the result of searchAnalyses() and fetching the analyses with fetchAnalyses().
tse
#> class: TreeSummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 1014 6 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(1014): sk__Bacteria sk__Bacteria;k__;p__Acidobacteria ...
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Poales;f__Poaceae;g__Triticum
#>   sk__Eukaryota;k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Solanales;f__Solanaceae;g__Nicotiana;s__Nicotiana_attenuata
#> rowData names(8): superkingdom kingdom ... genus species
#> colnames(6): MGYA00383350 MGYA00383351 ... MGYA01026512 MGYA01026513
#> colData names(16): analysis_accession study_accession ...
#>   sample_updated_at abundance_table
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> rowLinks: NULL
#> rowTree: NULL
#> colLinks: NULL
#> colTree: NULL

# Select analyses and fetch them
analyses <- searchAnalyses("MGYS00005116")
analyses <- analyses[analyses[["pipeline_version"]] == "V5", ]
tse <- fetchAnalyses(analyses)

# \donttest{
# Fetch a functional profile of a study
tse <- fetchStudies("MGYS00005610", type = "GO-slim")
#> Fetching 2 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.

# Fetch taxonomic and functional profiles into MultiAssayExperiment
mae <- fetchStudies("MGYS00005610", type = c("SSU", "GO-slim"))
#> Fetching 2 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.

# Browse studies and fetch them
studies <- searchStudies(biome = "root:Host-associated:Human", max.hits = 5)
tse <- fetchStudies(studies)
#> Fetching 6 analyses one by one, because they are missing from the summary tables of studies. This can take a while.
#> Could not download 6 tables: 'https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/metagenomics/mgnify_results/ERP001/ERP001506/version_1.0/ERS149129_A_SFF/otus/rdp_assigned_taxonomy/ERS149129_A_SFF_rRNAFiltered.fasta_rep_set_tax_assignments.txt', 'https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/metagenomics/mgnify_results/ERP001/ERP001506/version_1.0/ERS149130_A_SFF/otus/rdp_assigned_taxonomy/ERS149130_A_SFF_rRNAFiltered.fasta_rep_set_tax_assignments.txt', 'https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/metagenomics/mgnify_results/ERP001/ERP001506/version_1.0/ERS149131_A_SFF/otus/rdp_assigned_taxonomy/ERS149131_A_SFF_rRNAFiltered.fasta_rep_set_tax_assignments.txt', .... They might be missing from the server, or the server did not respond. If the server did not respond, try again later; only the missing tables are downloaded again.
#> No SSU abundance table could be fetched for 6 analyses (no such table, or it could not be downloaded): 'MGYA00002902', 'MGYA00002903', 'MGYA00002904', 'MGYA00002905', 'MGYA00002906', 'MGYA00002907'
#> The data includes analyses from multiple pipeline versions (V1, V2). Their profiles are based on different reference databases. Consider subsetting the result of searchAnalyses() and fetching the analyses with fetchAnalyses().
